input.question:
PROJECT INFORMATION
All dates are in 2026. All dates and times are local to America/Los_Angeles.
The project may run on October 19 and October 20 only.
Working hours on each day are 09:00–12:00 and 13:00–17:00. Lunch is 12:00–13:00.
The project deadline is October 20 at 17:00.
Every task A through N must be completed.

BASELINE PERSONNEL AVAILABILITY
Alex:

October 19: 09:00–12:00 and 13:00–16:00.
October 20: 09:00–12:00 and 13:00–17:00. Maya:
October 19: 10:00–12:00 and 13:00–17:00.
October 20: 09:00–12:00 and 14:00–17:00. Ethan:
October 19: 09:00–12:00 and 13:00–17:00.
October 20: 09:00–11:00 and 13:00–17:00.
BASELINE SHARED RESOURCE AVAILABILITY
GPU:

October 19: 10:00–12:00 and 13:00–17:00.
October 20: 09:00–12:00 and 13:00–17:00. Review Room:
October 19: 11:00–12:00 and 14:00–16:00.
October 20: 10:00–12:00 and 14:00–17:00. There is exactly one GPU and exactly one Review Room.
TASKS
Each task requires every listed person and resource simultaneously for its entire duration. A dash means no shared resource or no prerequisite, as applicable.

Task | Duration | People | Shared resources | Prerequisites | Additional cost
A | 1 hour | Alex, Maya | Review Room | - | 0
B | 1.5 hours | Alex | - | A | 0
C | 1 hour | Ethan | - | A | 0
D | 2 hours | Ethan | GPU | B, C | 0
E | 1.5 hours | Maya | - | A | 0
F | 1 hour | Alex, Ethan | - | D | 0
G, Standard | 2 hours | Ethan | GPU | F | 0
G, Accelerated | 1 hour | Ethan | GPU | F | 4
H | 1 hour | Maya | - | E, F | 0
I | 0.5 hours | Maya, Ethan | Review Room | G, H | 0
J | 0.5 hours | Alex | - | I | 0
K | 0.5 hours | Maya | - | I | 0
L | 0.5 hours | Ethan | GPU | J, K | 0
M | 0.5 hours | Alex, Maya | Review Room | L | 0
N | 0.5 hours | Ethan | GPU | M | 0

For task G, select exactly one method: Standard or Accelerated.
A person or shared resource cannot be assigned to overlapping tasks.
Every task must run continuously without interruption. Tasks cannot span lunch or be split across days.
Task start times must fall on 30-minute boundaries.
A task may start at the exact time its final prerequisite finishes.

CHANGE LOG
Apply only changes explicitly marked APPROVED. An approved change overrides only the specific information it mentions; all other information remains in effect.

APPROVED:
On October 19, Ethan's afternoon availability changes to 14:00–17:00.
His morning availability remains unchanged.

PROPOSED:
Consider outsourcing task G so it takes only 30 minutes at no additional cost.
This proposal has not been approved.

APPROVED:
On October 19, the GPU's afternoon availability changes to 15:00–17:00.
Its morning availability and October 20 availability remain unchanged.

WITHDRAWN:
The proposal to skip task I has been withdrawn.

APPROVED:
Task M may start only on October 20 at or after 15:30.

PROPOSED:
If necessary, extend the deadline to October 20 at 17:30.
This proposal has not been approved.

SCENARIOS
Evaluate each scenario independently.

Scenario 1:
The additional-cost budget is 4.
Construct a valid schedule with the minimum additional cost.
Among schedules with that cost, choose the earliest completion time.
Report the feasibility verdict, selected testing method, additional cost, project completion time, and a schedule listing the date, start time, and end time for every task A through N. Explain why no cheaper valid schedule exists and why completion cannot be earlier at the minimum cost.

Scenario 2:
Reduce only the additional-cost budget to 3.
All other conditions are identical to Scenario 1.
Determine whether the project can be completed by the deadline. Justify your verdict.

expected_output.criteria: Accept any valid schedule achieving minimum additional cost and earliest completion. Enforce durations, prerequisites, personnel/resource availability, exclusivity, continuity, lunch/day boundaries, approved changes, budget, and deadline. Evaluate explanation accuracy separately, distinguishing availability windows from task intervals.
